subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Is the local mock Azure Responses probe plus focused resolver coverage sufficient proof for this resolver-layer auth-provider fix, or should live Azure credentials be required before merge?
rationale: The code change is narrow and source-backed, but it affects auth-provider routing and the contributor explicitly did not test a live Azure account credential exchange.

options.title: Accept resolver-layer proof
options.body: Treat the mock Responses probe and focused tests as sufficient because the changed code chooses provider ownership before network credentials are exchanged, then land after current-base CI is green.

options.title: Require live Azure proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted `openclaw models status --probe --probe-provider azure-openai-responses` or agent smoke using real Azure credentials before merge.

options.title: Pause for owner-boundary redesign
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want a different permanent contract for model-catalog aliases, suppressions, and provider ownership.

recommendation.title: Accept resolver-layer proof
recommendation.body: Treat the mock Responses probe and focused tests as sufficient because the changed code chooses provider ownership before network credentials are exchanged, then land after current-base CI is green.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenAI catalog and model-catalog history makes this the strongest routing/proof decision owner from the inspected history.
